subject: MAP: unit-econ sanity & eval gating for pilot
messages:
From: Alicia Stone <alicia@brightforge.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@brightforge.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T09:14:00Z
Subject: MAP kickoff + quick ask on tokens/$ assumptions

Aditya — great to meet yesterday. Jordan and I sketched the MAP and attached a first draft (BrightForge_MAP_v1.docx). Before we lock milestones, can you confirm whether your unit-econ guidance for pilots assumes: average tokens per request, caching hit rates, and batching latency targets? We're modeling both a 10k DAU and a 50k DAU scenario and the financials swing a lot based on those three inputs.

High level ask: can your team produce a short note with the assumptions you recommend we use for the MAP gate (tokens/$, expected batching uplift at 50 RPS, and safe latency SLOs) so our CFO can sign off on the pilot budget?

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Stone
VP Product, BrightForge

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Stone <alicia@brightforge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-12T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + quick ask on tokens/$ assumptions

Alicia — thanks for the MAP draft. Quick answers up front and we'll follow with a spreadsheet:

- Baseline tokens per request: 350 avg (in our experience for BrightForge-style summarization + context)
- Caching: expect a 20% prefix-cache hitrate on first-pass queries for pilot traffic (higher for repeated queries).
- Batching uplift: 15–25% token-cost reduction at ~50 RPS depending on request size; we recommend conservative 18% for MAP planning.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 450ms for interactive flows; if BrightForge needs stricter SLAs we can propose a dedicated pool.

I'll drop the token-econ-quickcalc and a short rationale in the shared Drive. cc'ing Laura and Neha for billing/procurement and cost-verification.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-13T08:31:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + quick ask on tokens/$ assumptions

Looping in more granular numbers for the MAP financial gate. Summary below (we'll attach the calc sheet to the Drive link):

Assumptions used (MAP gate conservative view):
- Avg tokens per request: 350 (incl. prompt + expected response)
- Daily active requests (pilot): 10,000 req/day (10k DAU scenario) and 50,000 req/day (50k DAU scenario)
- Caching hit rate: 20% (prefix cache)
- Effective batching reduction: 18% token-cost reduction at target throughput (assumes 50–60% batching efficiency across CPU/GPU lanes)
- Redwood hosted execution cost (internal run rate for model family): $0.0018 per 1K tokens (internal cost figure for MAP planning)

Quick calc (conservative):
- 10k DAU: requests/day=10,000 -> tokens/day = 10,000 * 350 = 3,500,000 tokens/day.
  - After 20% cache hit (saves token generation) -> billable tokens = 2,800,000.
  - After batching uplift (18% reduction) -> effective billable tokens = 2,296,000.
  - Daily cost = (2,296,000 / 1000) * $0.0018 = $4.13/day (~$125/month)

- 50k DAU: tokens/day raw = 17,500,000. After cache & batching -> effective billable tokens ~ 11,480,000.
  - Daily cost = (11,480,000 / 1000) * $0.0018 = $20.66/day (~$620/month)

Notes / risk items:
- If BrightForge uses longer generated outputs (avg tokens > 350) costs scale linearly.
- Batching uplift is workload dependent; if requests are highly varied the uplift could be as low as 8–10%.
- Cache behavior can be worse for highly personalized prompts.

Laura
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@brightforge.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Alicia Stone <alicia@brightforge.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-15T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + quick ask on tokens/$ assumptions

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying items for our finance team before we freeze the MAP gate: 
1) Can Redwood provide a defensible worst-case for tokens/$ if caching is negligible (0%) and batching doesn't materialize (0%)? Our CFO wants a stress-case.
2) What latency impact do you expect if we enable aggressive prefetching + batching to chase the 18% uplift?

Also attaching an internal list of 10 example workflows (attached in eval-prompt-set.md) — the output lengths vary quite a bit.

Jordan

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@brightforge.com>
Cc: Alicia Stone <alicia@brightforge.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-17T17:42:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + quick ask on tokens/$ assumptions

Jordan — quick stress-case and operational notes below. We're happy to put these into the MAP doc and lock with signature if they look OK.

Stress-case (0% cache, 0% batching):
- 10k DAU: tokens/day = 3,500,000 -> cost = (3,500,000/1000) * $0.0018 = $6.30/day (~$190/month)
- 50k DAU: tokens/day = 17,500,000 -> cost = $31.50/day (~$945/month)

Operational/latency notes:
- Enabling prefetching + batching to reach ~18% uplift typically adds ~30–80ms median overhead depending on model latency and request coalescing window. 95th may slip by ~50–120ms in peak variance.
- If BrightForge requires 95th < 350ms we should move to a dedicated pool (extra reserved capacity) — we'll include dedicated pool pricing as an optional line item in the MAP.
- Eval plan suggestion: 1) Run a 7-day pilot traffic replay with sampled production logs, 2) measure cache hit delta across identical prefixes, 3) run an A/B with batching enabled to verify real uplift. We'll contribute the tooling to replay logs and the prompt set (eval-prompt-set.md).

Next steps: we'll upload the token-econ-quickcalc.csv and a short paragraph for the MAP that states conservative gate assumptions (350 t/req, 20% cache, 18% batching uplift) + stress-case (0%/0%). If BrightForge wants a tighter SLA we can draft a dedicated capacity commit.

If that works, can Alicia/Eigen (finance) sign off by next Tue (2025-06-24) so procurement can start the PO?

— Aditya
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
